function: Learned resource control of an aerial link: MAPPO decides UAV-to-HAP subcarrier assignment jointly with UAV trajectory and offloading ratio; transmit power is not learned (p. 9-10).
system: One HAP, three UAVs, 75 IoT devices; NOMA uplink devices-to-UAV, OFDMA UAV-to-HAP; no RIS; antennas not stated; wavelength 0.125 m, about 2.4 GHz (p. 3-5, 11).
method: Multi-agent PPO (MAPPO-JSCC), reinforcement learning with centralized training and decentralized execution; single-layer 64-neuron actor and critic; SCA and Dinkelbach embedded (p. 9, 10, 12).
data_channel: Custom simulator: air-to-ground LoS/NLoS free-space path loss with elevation-dependent LoS probability, 1000 m x 1000 m area, random device positions; no dataset or measurement (p. 4-5, 11).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in the same setting of three UAVs and 75 devices; only the trade-off weight kappa (1, 2, 10) is varied across runs (p. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: single-agent PPO (SAPPO) and TD3 with fast numerical method (TD3-FNM). Fixed-rule: maximum power (MaxTP), minimum power (MinTP), average subcarrier allocation (AAS) (p. 12).
metrics: Average and total task completion time, sum energy consumption, average device-to-UAV and UAV-to-HAP data rates, training reward (p. 11-13).
complexity: Big-O orders for each subproblem and overall MAPPO complexity O(TAN + TN + KTAN + KTN); no runtime or FLOPs (p. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 4: "the ground-to-air path loss models for LoS and NLoS" - custom air-to-ground model (eqs. 7-12); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "We consider three UAVs and one HAP, and 75 sensing" - a single configuration; pp. 12-13 vary only kappa, with no new scenario, number of UAVs or devices at test time.
q3_support: p. 12: "TD3-FNM [32], we used the TD3-based DRL algorithm"; p. 12: "each UAV can obtain the same number of subcarriers"; p. 13: "Fig. 5 illustrates a comparison of the total task completion"
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall complexity of the algorithm is O(T AN + T N + KT AN + KT N )"
q5_support: p. 12: "Other necessary parameters are given in" Table I - no code or data link, custom simulation, no public dataset.
notes: Borderline on above_phy: the objective is task completion time with UAV trajectory and offloading (above PHY), but the DRL also learns subcarrier assignment of the aerial UAV-to-HAP OFDMA link (p. 9 'The DRL method is in charge of solving the UAV trajectory, computing offloading and subcarrier allocation decisions'; p. 10 action au[t]), so it passes rule 4 and fits area 6 (aerial resource control). Transmit power is solved by SCA and Dinkelbach, not learned. The ISAC wording refers to IoT sensing times optimized in closed form (p. 8), not radar sensing. q3 relies on TD3-FNM as the earlier learned baseline and MaxTP, MinTP, AAS as fixed-rule non-learned baselines; the paper does not say how its other variables are decided in those baselines, and SAPPO may be read as a variant of the proposed method.
